answer: The system resists Sybil attacks through hardware attestation: each identity is bound to one certified token whose embedded prism splits a test light pulse into a spectrum a sensor measures and matches to the pattern recorded at registration, within 2 percent. Every 30 days the token must forge a signed response to a random challenge in under 10 seconds, and auditors wander unannounced between sites to compare 5 percent of tokens in person. A clone has no matching pattern or key, so 100 fakes need 100 separate tokens and 100 separate renewals.
